manifest.title: AFIG Progressive-Prior Diagnostic
manifest.description: Evidence-backed status, failure diagnosis, and next experimental gates for the 64x16 progressive latent prior.

blocks.body:
## We have a viable progressive representation, but not yet a viable fixed-order prior

The 64x16 tokenizer reconstructs well and its matched joint prior is materially stronger than the 16x64 and 32x32 controls. The central remaining failure is the **42.30-FID penalty introduced by fixed-order autoregression**. Naive four-register concatenation worsens the result, so the next work should preserve 16-D physical registers and target conditioning and exposure directly.

## Optimizer overfit is visible, but it is not the decoded failure

Teacher-forced validation flow MSE turns upward around 10k-20k while rollout FID continues to improve through 40k. Early stopping at the validation minimum would have selected a much worse generator. The constant learning rate may still be refined later, but it does not explain why AR remains far behind the joint prior.

## Exposure error is distributed across the coarse prefix

Replacing progressively longer generated prefixes with real ones improves FID smoothly. Exact AR completions add substantial value to prefixes of length 1-8, but after 16 real registers the generated suffix slightly worsens the prefix-only image. This indicates both early/middle error propagation and late detail that is insufficiently aligned to the realized scaffold.

## A special first-token weight is not the leading fix

Token 1 already carries about **4.75%** of validation MSE, roughly three times its uniform token share, while tokens 1-8 carry about **29.2%**. Supplying the exact first token improves FID by only 1.43. Its high loss also includes irreducible entropy because BOS provides no image-specific context. If weighting is tested, use a modest normalized emphasis over the first 8-16 registers and judge decoded FID—not teacher-forced MSE.

## Position exists in the trunk, but should be tested as a direct head condition

Every target slot receives a unique learned absolute embedding before the causal trunk, alongside RoPE in attention. The diffusion head receives the resulting 512-D state and timestep, but no direct positional bypass. A clean control is `MLP([h_i, e_i, e_t])`, with the same slot embedding supplied to every AdaLN block. This tests identifiability at the stochastic head without removing positional information from attention or adding a second inconsistent position system.

## Token-dependent SNR is best pursued as rolling generation

Current training uses independent uniform time for each target with tensor-wide standardization. Slot standard deviations vary only 0.735-1.149, so marginal scale alone is unlikely to explain the AR gap. A position-dependent schedule should follow conditional innovation and the measured coarse-to-fine prefix curve, not merely slot variance. Rolling diffusion/diffusion-forcing can keep 16-D registers separate, give each history register its own noise/time embedding, and move a denoising frontier from coarse to fine.

## Recommended experiment order

1. Add a direct learned target-slot condition to the flow head and verify that slot-conditioned behavior changes.
2. Add a small noisy-history teacher-forcing control to test robustness to generated-prefix drift.
3. Implement rolling diffusion with per-register time/noise conditioning while retaining 16-D token heads.
4. Only afterward test modest prefix-aware weighting or per-slot scalar normalization if diagnostics still point there.

The block-4 result rules out concatenation as the useful shortcut; it does not rule out attention between separate noisy register states during denoising.

## Latent quality needs a scorecard, not one covariance statistic

Use decoder reconstruction floor, progressive prefix and spectral recovery, off-manifold decoder-noise sensitivity, joint-prior FID, conditional innovation by slot, and final rollout FID. Effective rank and correlation are structural descriptors: low rank may reflect useful progressive redundancy or a difficult density, so optimizing either directly would be unsafe.

## Caveats

FID differences below about 0.3 are treated as protocol noise. Cross-slot teacher-forced MSE includes different irreducible conditional floors. Reconstruction FID 7.22 uses the current 5k evaluation and is best read as a codec ceiling estimate, not as a precision comparison with older 10k reconstruction evaluations.

baseline_config.setting: 512 width; 12 causal trunk blocks; 6 conditional AdaLN flow blocks; 8 heads; MLP ratio 4
RMS QK normalization; 1-D RoPE; learned absolute target-position embedding
Uniform time per target; straight rectified-flow path; velocity target; unweighted MSE
One tensor-wide population mean and standard deviation
AdamW 1e-4; betas 0.9/0.995; decay 0.05 on Linear/Conv weights only; gradient clip 1.0
Batch 256; BF16; 1k warmup then constant LR; compile default/fullgraph; no dropout
50-step Heun; no EMA, CFG, or class conditioning
No min-SNR, logit-normal time sampling, timestep weights, or token weights

query.sql: SELECT dataset, row_order, key_1, key_2, x, y, z, note FROM reviewed_measurements ORDER BY dataset, row_order
query.description: Reads the 51 reviewed measurements materialized from the project metric JSON files and canonical design log; artifact datasets are documented reshapes of these rows.
